summary.intent: Close the race in issue #7365 where two concurrent addrConn.connect() calls both saw Idle and both ran tryAllAddrs, orphaning a transport, by keeping ac.mu held from the Idle check through the Connecting transition.
summary.issue_fit: Met. connect() and updateAddrs() now hand ac.mu to resetTransportAndUnlock(), which sets Connecting before releasing it, so a second connect() sees non-Idle. The caller-reported 100000-run flake measurement was not repeatable here.
summary.coverage: Complete merge-base diff (clientconn.go, +6/-7) reviewed with all callers of the renamed function and the onClose/GracefulClose path. Reviewer-executed focused run at the head: `go test -race -v -run 'Test/(ResetConnectBackoff|BackoffCancel|UpdateAddresses|Dial_OneBackoffPerRetryGroup)' .` passed. Three concurrency safety premises were verified in one awaited batch and all hold. The PR text and issue were supplied by the caller; the offline clone has no forge packet. No uncommitted changes.

observations.fact: updateAddrs' deferred GracefulClose now runs while the spawned goroutine may still hold ac.mu, but the old transport's onClose only blocks briefly and then returns early because its ctx was cancelled.

requirements.evidence: clientconn.go:914-922 connect() keeps ac.mu from the Idle check into resetTransportAndUnlock, which sets Connecting at clientconn.go:1261 before unlocking

tasks.premise: ac.mu is released exactly once on every resetTransportAndUnlock path and both callers hold it on entry.
The deferred GracefulClose in updateAddrs cannot deadlock against the goroutine now holding ac.mu.
No two connection attempts can run concurrently via connect()/updateAddrs().
